reference.question: \(f(x)=7\). What is \(f'(5)\)?
reference.solution:
Method 1: Use the constant-function rule

The derivative of a constant is \(0\).

Method 2: Use the horizontal graph

The graph of \(f(x)=7\) is the horizontal line \(y=7\), so its tangent at \((5,7)\) is that same line. Its slope is \(0\); since a derivative equals the tangent slope, \(f'(5)=0\).
